journey:corinth-red-christ.l: Pinakothek der Moderne (Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen), Munich, Germany

x.summary: In this late work, Corinth paints the Crucifixion in violent reds, as if the whole scene were soaked in blood and fire. A soldier drives the lance into Christ's side, another lifts the vinegar-soaked sponge, and the mourning Virgin and Saint John press close to a Christ whose body is built from thick, slashing strokes of brush and palette knife. Painted three years before the artist's death, it is one of the most intense religious paintings of the Weimar years.
facts: Corinth suffered a serious stroke in December 1911 that left him partly paralysed on his left side; afterwards his style loosened and took on many Expressionist qualities.
Between Christ's outstretched arms the sun blazes with sharp rays, and sky, lake and sun are all drenched in red; Corinth painted on wood rather than canvas, in the manner of old German altarpieces.
Corinth trained as a realist and Impressionist, but works like this made him an important bridge to German Expressionism.
